Commentary.Commentary: ...THE CHASE..

Netherlands blew hot and cold. They started well but Shariz Ahmad and Paul van Meekeren leaked runs. The job is done with the ball and to win this match, they have to play in T20 mode. Netherlands do have some power but against the mighty Aussies, it won't be easy. Let's see how the second half pans out.

Australia will be happy with this score. They did a lot of shuffling to the line-up and gave a couple of players a test. David Warner was rested but Steven Smith did the job on top with a fine fifty. However, didn't get much support as Australia kept losing wickets at the other end. Alex Carey and Cameron Green got a start but just when they tried to move on they fell. Mitchell Starc was sent up the order and was mighty impressive as well.
Two to end! A brilliant last over by Paul. A full toss on middle, this is heaved towards deep mid-wicket.

Commentary.Commentary: The wait is over. We are all set. The players are out in the middle. David Warner is not padded up so Australia will go with a different combination. Steven Smith and Josh Inglis it is. Aryan Dutt to open with the ball.

Netherlands (SQUAD) - Scott Edwards (C/WK), Max O'Dowd, Bas de Leede, Vikramjit Singh, Teja Nidamanuru, Paul van Meekeren, Colin Ackermann, Roelof van der Merwe, Logan van Beek, Aryan Dutt, Ryan Klein, Wesley Barresi, Saqib Zulfiqar, Shariz Ahmad, Sybrand Engelbrecht.

Australia (SQUAD) - Mitchell Marsh, David Warner, Steven Smith, Marnus Labuschagne, Josh Inglis, Alex Carey (WK), Glenn Maxwell, Cameron Green, Marcus Stoinis, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins (C), Sean Abbott, Adam Zampa.

Scott Edwards says they would have bowled first. Adds last year's T20I World Cup was a success and had a good qualification tournament as well. Shares they want to play good cricket and informs, they are playing 12 players.
Pat Cummins says there is no particular reason to bat first. Adds they are pumped for the tournament and are well prepared. Informs a couple of their players are injured or rested.
TOSS - Australia have won the toss and will BAT.
Toss will be taking place at 1845 and first ball to be bowled at 1900 IST.
We have even better news! It is going to be a 23 over game.
Update - 5.30 pm IST (12 pm GMT) - All the covers have been removed but we still wait for an official word. Let's hope we get some news soon and action to see.
Most of the covers are off and it's quite bright now but not sure how dry it is. Keeping fingers crossed at the moment.
Update - 4 pm IST (10.30 am GMT) - The next inspection is at 4.30 pm IST. Few of the big covers have been removed but the pitch is still under cover. Let's hope for some good news.

Update - 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT) - The rain has completely stopped but the ground is still under covers. The groundsmen are working hard. It'll take time to get things ready but still it's looking a lot more positive. Stay tuned.
Update - 3 pm IST (9.30 am GMT) - The rain has eased down a bit and there will be an another inspection at 3.30 pm IST.
We will have an inspection at 1500 IST. It is still raining though and groundsmen will also need three hours to clear things up if the rain stops now.
Update (1400 IST) - The rain continues to pour, probably not as heavy as before but still coming down. There is a lot of water on the covers and the wait continues.
Not good news to begin with, it is raining here and it is consistent rain. The TOSS HAS BEEN DELAYED! To add to this, there are a lot of puddles on the ground at the moment. Not good signs.

It is time for another warm up game before the World Cup begins. This is a clash between the Aussies and Netherlands. Thr Australians are the most successful side when it comes to the 50-over World Cup and will be eager to have another successful campaign. They had a confidence boosting win against India in the last ODI of the series and are expected to win this one too. For Netherlands, it is a good chance to get an idea about their combination. They would love to give the Aussies a run for their money but it's not going to be easy.
... MATCH DAY ...
